cu_block._note: cooler A: flat face on the SoC (paste or PTM7950), face over the LPDDR5 recessed by ram_recess for a Gelid pad (STACK 5.8: never one pad over SoC and RAM); SoC and LPDDR5 tops from the Q6A STEP V1.21 (parts.json q6a); gap_tol is an assumed package/flatness tolerance (TBD); the block stays inside the keep-in of parts.json q6a_cooler_zone; fan_above_board = board top face to the fan's board-side face (>=10 per parts.json q6a_cooler_zone, +0.5 over the 9.65 mm 40-pin header); the fins/spacer between the 5 mm block and the fan and the fan bracket on the 58 x 49 holes are TBD with the purchased cooler

hdmi_route._src: W2 MECH-4 (B-04, build/15 'Кабель HDMI (W2 MECH-4)'): the FPC set of STACK.md:269 replaces the round Adafruit 2420 route (it needed a right-angle plug without an MPN and had no room for two Fair-Rite 0431164281 or the S-fold of about 250 mm of excess cable). Parts read 2026-11-07 (parts.json adafruit_3550, adafruit_3548, adafruit_flex, wurth_74278011). The flex keeps its width direction through bends; the two width changes (x at the Q6A receptacle, y at the Wisecoco input) and the x offset below the Q6A are made by three 45-degree folds (fold rating not published by Adafruit: fold once over a radius, never re-crease; bench OPEN) and the HDMI_INSERT is a straight pass-through between two 100 mm flexes (plan decision of W2 GR-4); segment centrelines (points) give the flex length: polyline + 2 x bend_r x (2 - pi/2) saved per 90-degree bend is ignored, so the length is an upper bound; slack = flex length - centreline <= slack_max, taken up as loose bends in hdmi_route_rise and hdmi_route_front_rise. MODEL ESTIMATE
hdmi_route._status: R-HDMI-ROUTE: envelopes of the 3550, the folds, the ferrite, the insert and the 3548 are in the envelope check (generated/fit-report.json); the HDMI link, the EMI effect of the unshielded flex with its grounded copper wrap and the ferrite, and the folds stay bench OPEN
